samples.summary: Browser login now hard-fails if the user spends more than 5 minutes at GitHub
samples.evidence: `CliAuthStore.createState` sets `expiresAt: Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000` (cli-auth.store.ts:39) and `githubAuthCallback` now throws `BadRequestException('Login state expired or invalid…')` for every callback whose state has expired (auth.controller.ts:130-135). Before this change the browser flow carried no state at all and always completed. A first-time user who has to sign in to GitHub, do 2FA, verify an email, or click through the app-authorization screen can easily exceed 5 minutes; they now get a 400 instead of a session. The TTL was chosen for a CLI flow that is scripted and fast, and is being reused unchanged for the interactive browser flow.

samples.summary: Browser login now depends on per-process in-memory state: a restart or a second backend instance breaks it
samples.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` stores the web flow's state in `CliAuthStore`, a plain `Map` on a singleton provider (`cli-auth.store.ts:24`, registered in `auth.module.ts:30`). `githubAuthCallback` refuses any callback whose token is not in that map (auth.controller.ts:131). The state is created on the instance that served `GET /auth/github` and looked up on the instance that serves `GET /auth/github/callback` — which behind a load balancer (no sticky sessions; GitHub's redirect is a fresh navigation) is frequently a different process, and after any deploy/restart is a different process for every in-flight login. Previously only the CLI flow had this coupling; now the primary browser login inherits it and fails closed with a 400.

samples.summary: User record is created before the state token is validated, so a rejected callback still has a persistent side effect
samples.evidence: `githubAuthCallback` calls `this.userService.findOrCreateUser({...})` at line 107-112, and only then checks `stateToken`/`consumeState` at lines 124-135. Every callback that is subsequently refused with `BadRequestException` (missing, forged, expired or replayed state) has already created (or touched) a user row for the GitHub identity that produced the code. The new validation should run before the side-effecting write.

samples.summary: Single-use state makes a reload/back-navigation of the callback URL a 400 instead of a re-login
samples.evidence: `consumeState` deletes the entry unconditionally (cli-auth.store.ts:53). The callback URL sits in browser history after the 302 to `FRONTEND_URL`; a user who presses Back (or reloads a restored tab) re-issues `GET /auth/github/callback?code=…&state=…` and now receives `BadRequestException('Login state expired or invalid…')` rather than the previous behaviour of re-setting cookies and redirecting. New user-visible failure mode introduced by this change.

samples.summary: Every unauthenticated hit on /auth/github now allocates a 5-minute state entry, and cleanup is O(n) per allocation
samples.evidence: The new fall-through at github-auth.guard.ts:91 calls `createState('web', 0)` for *every* request to `GET /auth/github` — including crawlers, prefetchers and anything hammering the endpoint — whereas before, non-CLI requests allocated nothing. `createState` then calls `cleanup()` (cli-auth.store.ts:41), which walks the entire `states` and `codes` maps on each call, so N concurrent starts cost O(N^2). Entries live 5 minutes each. The global per-IP `ThrottlerGuard` bounds a single source, but not many sources; this is a new unbounded-growth/CPU path on an unauthenticated endpoint.

samples.summary: The 30s callback timer is never cleared on the listener's failure path, so a failed `login` hangs the process for 30s
samples.evidence: `setTimeout(...)` at login.ts:443 is only cleared inside the returned `close()` (line 472), which is only reachable after the outer promise `resolve(...)` at line 468. On the `srv.on('error')` path (line 479-485) the outer promise is `reject`ed and `close()` is never handed to a caller, so the un-`unref`'d 30s timer keeps the Node event loop alive: `wafflebase login` prints its error envelope and then sits for ~30 seconds before exiting. The timer should be `clearTimeout`ed (or `unref`ed) on the reject path too.

`isLoopbackHost` matches the host against `/^(\[[^\]]+\]|[^:]+)(?::(\d+))?$/`. A bare `::1` matches neither alternative (`[^:]+` cannot contain a colon), so `match` is null and the function returns false before ever consulting the set. The `'::1'` member of `LOOPBACK_HOSTS` (line 276) is therefore dead — only `'[::1]'` is reachable — and a client sending `Host: ::1` is rejected despite the set claiming otherwise.

samples.summary: Stale comment still refers to the removed `__cliStateToken` and to CLI-only state
samples.evidence: auth.controller.ts:89-94 still says "For CLI mode, the state token is injected in the guard via __cliStateToken". The property was renamed to `__oauthStateToken` (github-auth.guard.ts:84/92, github.strategy.ts:65) and state is now injected for the browser flow too, so the comment describes behaviour that no longer exists.

finding.summary: Browser login now hard-fails if the user spends more than 5 minutes at GitHub
finding.evidence: `CliAuthStore.createState` sets `expiresAt: Date.now() + 5 * 60 * 1000` (cli-auth.store.ts:39) and `githubAuthCallback` now throws `BadRequestException('Login state expired or invalid…')` for every callback whose state has expired (auth.controller.ts:130-135). Before this change the browser flow carried no state at all and always completed. A first-time user who has to sign in to GitHub, do 2FA, verify an email, or click through the app-authorization screen can easily exceed 5 minutes; they now get a 400 instead of a session. The TTL was chosen for a CLI flow that is scripted and fast, and is being reused unchanged for the interactive browser flow.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present exactly as described. cli-auth.store.ts:39 hardcodes a 5-minute TTL in createState with no mode parameterization. github-auth.guard.ts:91 is the browser fall-through path and now calls createState('web', 0), injecting OAuth state into every browser login (the guard's own comment at lines 52-54 confirms the 5-minute hold and that the browser flow previously had no state). auth.controller.ts:130-135 calls consumeState and throws BadRequestException when it returns undefined, which cli-auth.store.ts:49-52 does for any entry where expiresAt < Date.now(). That rejection sits above the `state.mode === 'cli'` branch at line 137, so it applies to the web flow identically, and it fires after findOrCreateUser at line 107 — the user is persisted but no session cookie is ever set. I enumerated all callers: createState only at github-auth.guard.ts:79 and :91; consumeState only at auth.controller.ts:130. There is no mode-aware TTL, no extension, and no fallback that lets an expired web callback complete, so 'already-guarded' does not apply. A realistic interactive path (first-time GitHub signup, 2FA, email verification, app-authorization screen) can exceed 5 minutes and yields a 400 instead of a session, breaking the core login flow. This is a boundary/threshold value reused for a path it was not sized for, which is squarely in the correctness lane rather than style or architecture; the fact that the failure is a graceful 400 rather than a crash makes it recoverable but does not make it non-blocking.

finding.summary: Browser login now depends on per-process in-memory state: a restart or a second backend instance breaks it
finding.evidence: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` stores the web flow's state in `CliAuthStore`, a plain `Map` on a singleton provider (`cli-auth.store.ts:24`, registered in `auth.module.ts:30`). `githubAuthCallback` refuses any callback whose token is not in that map (auth.controller.ts:131). The state is created on the instance that served `GET /auth/github` and looked up on the instance that serves `GET /auth/github/callback` — which behind a load balancer (no sticky sessions; GitHub's redirect is a fresh navigation) is frequently a different process, and after any deploy/restart is a different process for every in-flight login. Previously only the CLI flow had this coupling; now the primary browser login inherits it and fails closed with a 400.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real (browser state created at github-auth.guard.ts:91-92 into the in-memory Map at cli-auth.store.ts:24, singleton at auth.module.ts:30, required at auth.controller.ts:130-135), but the claimed blocking impact is a deployment/statelessness architecture concern, not a logic or runtime correctness defect, and it is outside the Correctness lane. (a) No multi-instance topology exists in this repo: single Nest process (main.ts:31, no cluster/fork), one container CMD (Dockerfile:93), docker-compose runs only postgres/yorkie/minio, and no k8s/helm/deploy manifests exist — the "load balancer without sticky sessions" premise is supplied by the reviewer, not the repository. (b) The process-affinity assumption is pre-existing and system-wide: cliExchange already consumes an in-memory code from the same store (auth.controller.ts:165, cli-auth.store.ts:69-77), so no new invariant is broken by the code itself. (c) The restart case fails closed with a clear retryable 400 (auth.controller.ts:132-134) — no crash, no data loss, no dropped await, no incorrect condition. Under this lens's rubric (wrong conditions, off-by-one, null crashes, async mistakes, data loss, broken invariants), there is nothing logically wrong in the code path as written; horizontal-scalability of the OAuth state store is architecture/design fit, explicitly deferred.

finding.summary: `GET /start` is single-use and method-agnostic, so any duplicate/speculative request silently breaks the login for 30s
finding.evidence: `if (startConsumed) { res.writeHead(410) … }` at login.ts:272-276 marks the redirect consumed on the *first* request of any kind, before the browser has necessarily navigated. Real, non-adversarial duplicates exist: (a) a HEAD/preview/URL-scanner request (the handler never checks `req.method`, so HEAD consumes it), (b) omnibox/link prefetch when the user copy-pastes the printed `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start` — the very headless path the comment at login.ts:52-65 says must keep working, (c) the user reloading or hitting Back and retrying after a hiccup, (d) a browser launcher that issues the URL twice. In all of these the real navigation gets `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, no `/callback` ever arrives, and the CLI blocks the full 30s (login.ts:373-385) before failing with the generic `Login timed out` — with no hint that the one-time link was burnt. The previous code passed the authorize URL directly to `open()` and had no such failure mode, so this is a newly introduced hang/regression on ordinary paths.

verdict.reason: The finding describes a single-use, method-agnostic `GET /start` redirect handler that does not exist in this repository. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts (490 lines) contains no `startConsumed`, no `START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, and no `res.writeHead(410)`; grepping packages/ for `startConsumed|START_CONSUMED|/start` and `writeHead\(410` returns only two hits, both inside a doc comment (login.ts:175, 182). The request handler recognizes exactly one path — `if (url.pathname !== '/callback') { res.writeHead(404) }` (login.ts:349-353) — so there is no `/start` route to consume. The current flow is precisely the one the finding claims was replaced: `buildAuthorizeUrl(...)` is handed straight to `open()` (login.ts:196-203) and is also the printed URL (login.ts:198), so the headless copy-paste path uses the authorize URL directly and no one-shot loopback link exists. The doc comment at login.ts:174-179 explicitly records that the `/start` 302 design was tried and abandoned for exactly the reason the reviewer restates, which is likely what was misread as live code. The cited evidence lines do not match: login.ts:270-273 is the `UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE` string constant, and login.ts:372-383 is the nonce-less-callback branch returning `400 UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE`, not a 410. The sub-claim that the handler never checks `req.method` is also contradicted by an explicit `if (req.method !== 'GET') { res.writeHead(405) }` guard at login.ts:341-345 placed before any path dispatch, which blocks HEAD/POST probes outright. With the described mechanism absent, the derived 30s hang/regression has no origin in this code.
